note: Ingest configuration for integrations/source_mirror.py: how a full sync pages the Portal Workbench reporting API and how each stored row's lineage is derived. Configuration, not authority. Sync limits mirror the service (petralabx/plx-customer-portal@b46934a services/workbench-api: query.mjs LIMITS maxLimit 5000 rows and 5 MB per page; wb_api 5 connections, 30 s statements, a sixth concurrent request gets 503 and should retry, docs/runbooks/WORKBENCH-API.md). max_rows_per_relation bounds one traversal (counted across the runs it resumes in) against a runaway read, never a real relation: measured 2026-10-29 the largest served relation, public.app_manufacturing_order_line, held 31,658,270 rows (the Portal ETL's per-run copies of 262,608 natural keys), read in about an hour at 8,776 rows/s; 64,000,000 is about twice that (integrations/source_mirror.py MAX_ROWS_PER_RELATION_CAP). Lineage rules are tried in order and the first match wins; a gold row with no exposed origin marker gets the C0 default gold_native_staging under rule gold_no_origin_marker (origin unproven; never authority until a human confirms it, Q1). Soft-delete rules declare the source's own deletion marker: a relation matching a rule's patterns whose catalog columns include its column labels a row with a value there deleted_in_source (never inferred from absence).

soft_delete_rules.evidence: Portal Prisma models soft-delete regulatory tables through deletedAt @map("deleted_at") (petralabx/plx-customer-portal@8b08c9e portal/prisma/schema.prisma design note 'Soft deletes on regulatory tables (deletedAt)'), and Portal's loaders read only deletedAt null (portal/src/lib/sales-order/load-order-lifecycle.ts@59b0548). The reporting API serves deleted_at on the gold relations whose catalog columns carry it (services/workbench-api/manifest/allowlist.json@5802e63); a relation qualifies by its catalog, never by name.
